nodes.label: IpamBox — self-hosted IPAM with built-in LAN scanner
nodes.rationale: Keeps the documented network and the real network in sync: model the address space, scan it, and drift shows up as data.

nodes.label: IPAM feature set (hierarchy, overlap safety, allocation, CSV, workbook import)
nodes.rationale: Consistency rules enforced by the database itself (GiST exclusion constraint, UNIQUE(vrf_id,address)), not by convention.

nodes.label: LAN scanner (ARP/ICMP/TCP/PTR/OUI reconciliation)
nodes.rationale: Reconciliation: new hosts land as discovered in the inbox, missing active hosts go offline, MAC disagreements flag mac_mismatch with the live value winning.

nodes.label: Architecture — web/api/scanner/db/redis services
nodes.rationale: Browser talks only to web; API calls go same-origin via a Next.js rewrite so there is no CORS. Scanner needs host networking (Linux only) for real L2 ARP.

nodes.label: Backup & restore (.json.gz snapshots)
nodes.rationale: Users table excluded by default because accounts belong to the server being restored on; admin accounts are never exported so a backup file can never carry admin credentials. Restores are atomic, ID-preserving and schema-checked.

nodes.label: 4-tier RBAC (Administrator/Operator/Contributor/Viewer)
nodes.rationale: Roles enforced on every API route, not just hidden in the UI; existing accounts migrate to Administrator on upgrade so nothing locks you out.

nodes.label: Ops endpoints (/healthz, /readyz, /metrics, /api/v1/*)
nodes.rationale: web :3010 and api :8001 are published on all interfaces deliberately for LAN scripting; API_BIND=127.0.0.1 restricts the API to loopback.

nodes.label: Rack elevations feature (front/rear U placement, Rackula round-trip)
nodes.rationale: Front+rear share a U because a cabinet has two faces; same-face overlaps are rejected. Round-trips with self-hosted Rackula for heavy editing instead of a built-in drag editor.
